summary:
MSERSP-01 (MARS SURFACE EMERGENCY RECOVERY & SURVIVAL PROTOCOL) — Team The Martians (Uzbekistan).

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, MSERSP-01 is an advanced digital command center and survival web application designed to manage life support, resource rationing, and safe surface evacuation under extreme Martian conditions (~0.6 kPa pressure, severe cold, and comms delay).

Key Features:

*Interactive 3D Globe & 2D Tactical Map: Seamless switching between a high-resolution 3D Mars sphere and a 2D tactical view with Apple Maps-style deep zoom and click-anywhere waypoint routing that automatically plots safe paths bypassing hazardous craters and slopes.


*Biometric Survival & Rescue ETA Calculator (Our Ace): Computes precise metabolic and water requirements using strict MSERSP-01 gender baselines. Features a one-click ration stretcher that dynamically distributes remaining supplies across exact Sols until rescue, safely clamped at survival floors.


*Resource Storage & Unit Toggles: Absolute tracking for food (kcal), water (L), and oxygen with seamless Metric and US Customary unit switching.
Built-In MSERSP-01 Digital Manual: Instant aerospace emergency handbook covering all 6 phases (Seal & Breathe, Power & Heat, Rationing, Comms, ISRU, and MAV Evacuation).



MSERSP-01 bridges authentic NASA mission standards with an intuitive interface to ensure crew survival on the Red Planet.
details:
Project Name: MSERSP-01 (MARS SURFACE EMERGENCY RECOVERY & SURVIVAL PROTOCOL) — Team The Martians (Uzbekistan)

Project Overview & Functionality: MSERSP-01 is an advanced, engineering-grade digital command center and survival web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It addresses the critical challenges of life support management, resource tracking, and safe surface evacuation under extreme Martian conditions (such as ~0.6 kPa surface pressure, severe temperature drops, and communication delays). The application acts as a real-time operational dashboard for stranded astronauts or mission control personnel.

How It Works & Core Features:

  1. Interactive 3D Globe & 2D Tactical Map: Features seamless switching between a high-resolution 3D Mars sphere and a 2D tactical view with Apple Maps-style deep zoom. Utilizing NASA MOLA topography data, clicking any arbitrary point on the map automatically plots the shortest safe route from the habitat base while intelligently bypassing hazardous craters and steep slopes.
  2. Biometric Survival & Rescue ETA Calculator (Our Ace Feature): Calculates personalized daily metabolic calorie (kcal/sol) and water (L/sol) requirements based on strict MSERSP-01 gender-specific baselines. It tracks absolute resource horizons and features an innovative "Rescue ETA Ration Stretcher" that dynamically redistributes remaining food and water evenly across the exact Sols until rescue, securely clamped at physiological survival floors.
  3. Food & Resource Storage Inventory: Provides absolute tracking for consumables (food in kcal, water in liters/gallons, and oxygen in kg/lbs) with instant toggles between Metric and US Customary units.
  4. Built-In MSERSP-01 Digital Manual: An instant aerospace emergency handbook integrated via a centered modal window, outlining all 6 critical survival phases (Seal & Breathe, Power & Heat Regulation, Resource Audit & Rationing, Communications & Positioning, In-Situ Resource Utilization - ISRU, and MAV Evacuation).

Tools, Technologies & Data Sources:

  • Frontend & Architecture: Built as a high-performance web application utilizing React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js for interactive planetary rendering.
  • NASA Open Data & Standards: Incorporated MOLA topographical slope data, SWIM subsurface water-ice mapping data for ISRU, and NASA human spaceflight metabolic/ECLSS baselines.
  • Design System: Engineered with a NASA-inspired dark basalt aesthetic, precision telemetry widgets, and aerospace UI components.

Project Impact & Creativity: MSERSP-01 bridges the gap between complex engineering emergency protocols and intuitive, stress-proof user interfaces. By combining spatial pathfinding with dynamic metabolic math, it transforms static survival manuals into an active decision-support tool, ensuring mission success and crew survival on the Red Planet.
